title.zh: 卷34 列傳第26 趙善 元定 楊摽 裴寬 楊敷
title.en: Volume 34 Biographies 26: Zhao Shan; Yuan Ding; Yang Biao; Pei Kuan; Yang Fu
title.raw: 卷34 列傳第26 趙善 元定 楊摽 裴寬 楊敷 Volume 34 Biographies 26: Zhao Shan; Yuan Ding; Yang Biao; Pei Kuan; Yang Fu

sentences.zh: 趙善字僧慶，太傅、楚國公貴之從祖兄也。

translations.literal: Zhao Shan, styled Sengqing, was a paternal cousin once removed of the Grand Tutor and Duke of Chu, Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shan, courtesy name Sengqing, was a senior cousin of Yuwen Gui, grand tutor and Duke of Chu.

sentences.zh: 祖國，魏龍驤將軍、洛州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guo was Wei General of Dragon Cavalry and Inspector of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guo had served Wei as general of dragon cavalry and inspector of Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 父更，安樂太守。

translations.literal: His father Geng was Administrator of Anle commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Geng was administrator of Anle commandery.

sentences.zh: 善少好學，涉獵經史，美容儀，沉毅有遠量。

translations.literal: Shan in youth loved learning, ranged through the classics and histories, had fine bearing, and was deep, resolute, and far-seeing.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shan loved learning and read widely in the classics and histories; he was handsome in bearing, grave and resolute, with a statesman's long view.

sentences.zh: 永安初，爾朱天光為肆州刺史，辟為主簿，深器重之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongan, Erzhu Tianguang was Inspector of Si Province; he summoned Shan as chief clerk and deeply valued him.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yongan era Erzhu Tianguang, then inspector of Si Province, recruited Shan as chief clerk and came to rely on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 天光討邢杲及万俟醜奴，以善為長史。

translations.literal: When Tianguang campaigned against Xing Gao and Moqi Chounu, he made Shan chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang marched against Xing Gao and Moqi Chounu, he appointed Shan chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 軍中謀議，每參預之。

translations.literal: In the army's counsels and deliberations, he took part in every one.
translations.idiomatic: He sat in on every council and plan the army devised.

sentences.zh: 天光為關右行臺，表善為行臺左丞，加都督、征虜將軍。

translations.literal: When Tianguang became mobile headquarters commissioner for the Guanxi region, he memorialized that Shan be made left assistant of the mobile headquarters, with the added titles area commander and General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang was made mobile headquarters commissioner for the Guanxi region, he recommended Shan as left assistant of the headquarters, with the additional titles area commander and general who campaigns against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，賞平關、隴之功，拜驃騎將軍、大行臺、散騎常侍，封山北縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai, in reward for pacifying Guan and Long, he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry, Great Mobile Headquarters commissioner, and Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry; he was enfeoffed Baron of Shanbei county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Putai he was rewarded for pacifying the Guan and Long regions with the posts of general of agile cavalry, great mobile headquarters commissioner, and regular attendant of scattered cavalry, and was enfeoffed Baron of Shanbei with five hundred fief households.

sentences.zh: 俄除持節、東雍州諸軍事、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed and made Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Eastern Yong Province, and Inspector of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was given bearer of the staff, made commander-in-chief of Eastern Yong Province, and appointed inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 天光東拒齊神武於韓

translations.literal: Tianguang went east to resist Gao Huan at Han
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang marched east to meet Gao Huan at Han

translations.literal: (Lìng) [emended: Líng]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Líng]

sentences.zh: 陵，善又以長史從。

translations.literal: 〔Líng〕, Shan again followed as chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: At Hanling, Shan again served as chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 及天光敗見殺，善請收葬其屍，齊神武義而許之。

translations.literal: When Tianguang was defeated and killed, Shan asked to gather and bury his corpse; Gao Huan, deeming it righteous, granted it.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianguang was defeated and executed, Shan asked permission to recover and bury his body; moved by the gesture, Gao Huan consented.

sentences.zh: 賀拔岳總關中兵，乃遣迎善，復以為長史。

translations.literal: Heba Yue commanded the Guanzhong armies; he thereupon sent to welcome Shan and again made him chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yue, who then held command in Guanzhong, sent for Shan and again made him chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 岳為侯莫陳悅所害，善共諸將翊戴太祖，仍從平悅。

translations.literal: When Yue was murdered by Houmochen Yue, Shan together with the other commanders supported and enthroned the Grand Progenitor; he still followed in the pacification of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: After Houmochen Yue murdered Heba Yue, Shan and the other generals rallied behind Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai and marched with him to crush Houmochen Yue.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，除都官尚書，改封襄城縣伯，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Shan was appointed Minister of Justice; his fief was changed to Baron of Xiangcheng county, with five hundred additional households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu withdrew westward, Shan was made minister of justice, his title was changed to Baron of Xiangcheng, and his fief was increased by five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 頃之，為北道行臺，與儀同李虎等討曹泥，克之。

translations.literal: Before long he became mobile headquarters commissioner for the northern route; together with Yitong Li Hu and others he campaigned against Cao Ni and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made mobile headquarters commissioner for the northern route and, with Li Hu and others, marched against Cao Ni and took him.

sentences.zh: 遷車騎大將軍、儀同三司、尚書右僕射，進爵為公，增邑幷前一千五百戶。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Yitong of the Three Precedences, and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat; he was advanced in rank to duke, and his fief together with the former totaled one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand general of chariots and cavalry, yitong of the Three Precedences, and right vice director of the Secretariat, advanced to duke, and given a combined fief of one thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，轉左僕射，兼侍中，監著作，領太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, he was transferred to Left Vice Director, concurrently Palace Attendant, overseer of the Bureau of Compilation, and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 3 he became left vice director, with concurrent posts as palace attendant, overseer of the bureau of compilation, and grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 善性溫恭，有器局，雖位居端右，而逾自謙退。

translations.literal: Shan by nature was warm and respectful, with capacity and breadth; though his rank stood at the summit, he became ever more self-effacing.
translations.idiomatic: Shan was warm and courteous by nature, with the breadth of a true minister; though he stood at the pinnacle of office, he grew only more modest.

sentences.zh: 其職務克舉，則曰某官之力；

translations.literal: When his duties were fully accomplished, he would say it was the strength of such-and-such an office;
translations.idiomatic: When affairs went well he would say the credit belonged to the office itself;

sentences.zh: 若有罪責，則曰善之咎也。

translations.literal: if there were fault or blame, he would say it was Shan's fault.
translations.idiomatic: when something went wrong he would say the fault was his alone.

sentences.zh: 時人稱其公輔之量。

translations.literal: Men of the time praised his measure as befitting a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised him as having the stature of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 太祖亦雅敬重焉。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor also always held him in deep respect.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai likewise held him in deep esteem.

sentences.zh: 九年，從戰邙山，屬大軍不利，善為敵所獲，遂卒於東魏。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he followed the campaign at Mount Mang; as the great army met misfortune, Shan was captured by the enemy and thereupon died in Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he fought at Mount Mang; when the main force was routed he was taken by the enemy and died in Eastern Wei captivity.

sentences.zh: 建德初，朝廷與齊通好，齊人乃歸其柩。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiande, the court and Qi restored friendly relations; the men of Qi then returned his coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiande era, as the court and Northern Qi renewed friendly ties, Qi returned his coffin.

sentences.zh: 其子絢表請贈諡。

translations.literal: His son Xuan memorialized requesting a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan petitioned for a posthumous honorific.

sentences.zh: 詔贈大將軍、大都督、岐宜寧豳四州諸軍事、岐州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously awarded him Grand General, Grand Area Commander, Commander-in-Chief of Qi, Yi, Ning, and Bin provinces, and Inspector of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The throne posthumously made him grand general and grand area commander, commander-in-chief of Qi, Yi, Ning, and Bin, and inspector of Qi.

sentences.zh: 諡曰敬。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Jing.

sentences.zh: 子度，字幼濟，車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: His son Du, styled Youji, was Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Yitong of the Three Precedences.
translations.idiomatic: His son Du, courtesy name Youji, rose to grand general of chariots and cavalry and yitong of the Three Precedences.

sentences.zh: 度弟絢，字會績，驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、淅資二州刺史。

translations.literal: Du's younger brother Xuan, styled Huiji, was General of Agile Cavalry, Opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, and Inspector of Xi and Zi provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Du's younger brother Xuan, courtesy name Huiji, became general of agile cavalry, opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, and inspector of Xi and Zi provinces.

sentences.zh: 元定字願安，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Ding, styled Yuan'an, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ding, courtesy name Yuan'an, came from Luoyang in Henan commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖比頹，魏安西將軍、務州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bi Tui was Wei General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Wu Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bi Tui had served Wei as general who pacifies the west and inspector of Wu Province.

sentences.zh: 父道龍，征虜將軍、鉅鹿郡守。

translations.literal: His father Daolong was General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Administrator of Julu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daolong was general who campaigns against the barbarians and administrator of Julu commandery.

sentences.zh: 定惇厚少言，內沉審而外剛毅。

translations.literal: Ding was honest and thick, spoke little; inwardly deep and careful, outwardly firm and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was plain, steadfast, and sparing of speech — inwardly thoughtful and cautious, outwardly hard and resolute.

sentences.zh: 永安初，從爾朱天光討關隴羣賊，並破之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongan, he followed Erzhu Tianguang in campaigning against the bandit hosts of Guan and Long and broke them all.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Yongan he marched with Erzhu Tianguang against the rebel armies of Guan and Long and defeated them all.

sentences.zh: 除襄

translations.literal: He was removed and made
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed

translations.literal: (Rong) [emended: Wei]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Wei]

sentences.zh: 〔威〕將軍。

translations.literal: 〔Wei〕 General.
translations.idiomatic: general who pacifies the distant.

sentences.zh: 及賀拔岳被害，定從太祖討侯莫陳悅，以功拜平遠將軍、步兵校尉。

translations.literal: When Heba Yue was murdered, Ding followed the Grand Progenitor in campaigning against Houmochen Yue; for merit he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant and Commandant of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: After Heba Yue was killed, Ding followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai against Houmochen Yue and, for his service, was made general who pacifies the distant and commandant of footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，封高邑縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Ding was enfeoffed Baronet of Gaoyi county with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu withdrew westward, Ding was enfeoffed Baronet of Gaoyi with two hundred fief households.

sentences.zh: 從擊潼關，拔回洛城，進爵為伯，增邑三百戶，加前將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: He followed in the assault on Tong Pass, captured Huiluo city, was advanced in rank to baron with three hundred additional households, and was given the added titles General of the Van and Grand Master of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Tong Pass, helped take Huiluo, was raised to baron with three hundred additional households, and received the added ranks of general of the van and grand master of palace attendance.

sentences.zh: 從擒竇泰，復弘農，破沙苑，戰河橋，定皆先鋒，當其前者，無不披靡。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Dou Tai, the recovery of Hongnong, the victory at Shaye, and the battle at Heqiao; in every engagement Ding was vanguard, and whoever stood before him was swept aside without exception.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in capturing Dou Tai, retaking Hongnong, winning at Shaye, and fighting at Heqiao; in each battle Ding led the van, and no one who faced him held the line.

sentences.zh: 以前後功，累遷都督、征東將軍、金紫光祿大夫、帥都督，增邑三百戶。

translations.literal: For successive merits he was repeatedly promoted to area commander, General Who Campaigns East, Grand Master with the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, and chief area commander, with three hundred additional fief households.
translations.idiomatic: For repeated victories he rose step by step to area commander, general who campaigns east, grand master with the gold seal and purple ribbon, and chief area commander, with three hundred more fief households.

sentences.zh: 邙山之役，敵人如堵，定奪矟沖之，殺傷甚衆，無敢當者。

translations.literal: At the battle of Mount Mang the enemy stood thick as a wall; Ding seized a spear and charged them, killing and wounding a great host, and none dared stand against him.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Mang the enemy massed like a wall; Ding snatched a spear and drove straight in, killing and wounding a great many, and no one dared meet him.

sentences.zh: 太祖親觀之，論功為最，賞物甚厚。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor watched in person; in reckoning merit he ranked first, and the reward of goods was very rich.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai watched from the field; when merits were counted Ding stood first, and his reward was lavish.

sentences.zh: 十三年，授河北郡守，加大都督、通直散騎常侍，增邑通前一千戶。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed Administrator of Hebei commandery, with the added titles Grand Area Commander and Direct Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry; his fief together with the former totaled one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was made administrator of Hebei commandery, given the added titles grand area commander and direct regular attendant of scattered cavalry, and granted a combined fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 定有勇略，每戰必陷陣，然未嘗自言其功。

translations.literal: Ding had courage and stratagem; in every battle he broke the enemy line, yet he never spoke of his own merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was brave and resourceful and always punched through the enemy formation, yet he never claimed credit for himself.

sentences.zh: 太祖深重之，諸將亦稱其長者。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor deeply valued him, and the other commanders also praised him as an elder worthy of respect.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai held him in the highest regard, and the other generals spoke of him as a man of senior stature.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷使持節、車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為公。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Opener of the Way with the Three Precedences; he was advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was given bearer of the staff and promoted to grand general of chariots and cavalry and opener of the Way with the Three Precedences, and raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，以宗室，進封建城郡王。

translations.literal: In the second year of the deposed Emperor of Wei, because of his imperial clan status, he was advanced and enfeoffed Prince of Jiancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Fei, as a member of the imperial clan he was advanced and enfeoffed Prince of Jiancheng commandery.

translations.literal: (Two) [emended: Three]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Three]

sentences.zh: ［三］年，行《周禮》，爵隨例改，封長湖郡公。

translations.literal: 〔Three〕 year, when the Rites of Zhou were implemented, ranks changed according to precedent; he was enfeoffed Duke of Changhu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when the Zhou Rites were put into practice and titles were revised by precedent, he was enfeoffed Duke of Changhu commandery.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，拜岷州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign he was appointed Inspector of Min Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign he was made inspector of Min Province.

sentences.zh: 威恩兼濟，甚得羌豪之情。

translations.literal: Authority and kindness together reached the people; he won the hearts of the Qiang chieftains exceedingly.
translations.idiomatic: He combined firm authority with kindness and won the Qiang chieftains over completely.

sentences.zh: 先時生羌據險不賓者，至是並出山谷，從征賦焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, live Qiang who held the passes and would not submit — at this time all came out from the valleys and followed the levies and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang who had long held the mountain passes now came down from the hills and submitted to taxation and corvée.

sentences.zh: 及定代還，羌豪等感戀之。

translations.literal: When Ding was replaced and returned, the Qiang chieftains were moved and clung to him in longing.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding was recalled and left his post, the Qiang chieftains were grief-stricken at his departure.

sentences.zh: 保定中，授左宮伯中大夫。

translations.literal: In the Baoding era he was appointed Senior Master of the Left Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoding he was made senior master of the left palace guard.

sentences.zh: 久之，轉左武伯中大夫，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to Senior Master of the Left Martial Guard and advanced in rank to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to senior master of the left martial guard and promoted to grand general.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，陳湘州刺史華皎舉州歸梁，梁主欲因其隙，更圖攻取，乃遣使請兵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, Hua Jiao, Inspector of Xiang Province in Chen, raised the province and submitted to Liang; the Liang ruler wished to use the opening to press further attacks and seize more, and so sent envoys requesting troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe year 2, Hua Jiao, Chen's inspector of Xiang Province, defected with his province to Liang; the Liang emperor meant to exploit the breach and sent envoys asking for Zhou troops.

sentences.zh: 詔定從衛公直率衆赴之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ding to follow the Duke of Wei Zhi and lead troops to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Ding to march under Duke of Wei Yuwen Zhi to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 梁人與華皎皆為水軍，定為陸軍，直總督之，俱至夏口。

translations.literal: The men of Liang and Hua Jiao were both river forces; Ding was the land force; Zhi overall commanded them; together they reached Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Hua Jiao fielded river fleets while Ding led the land army under Zhi's overall command; all reached Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 而陳郢州堅守不下。

translations.literal: But Chen's Ying Province held firm and would not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ying Province in Chen held out and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 直令定率步騎數千圍之。

translations.literal: Zhi ordered Ding to lead several thousand infantry and cavalry to invest it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi ordered Ding to invest the city with several thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 陳遣其將淳于量、徐度、吳明徹等水陸來拒。

translations.literal: Chen sent its commanders Chunyu Liang, Xu Du, Wu Mingche, and others by land and water to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Chen dispatched Chunyu Liang, Xu Du, Wu Mingche, and others by land and water to block them.

sentences.zh: 量等以定已度江，勢分，遂先與水軍交戰。

translations.literal: Liang and the others, because Ding had already crossed the river and his force was divided, thereupon first joined battle with the river army.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Ding had already crossed the Yangzi and his force was split, Liang and the others struck first at the river fleet.

sentences.zh: 而華皎所統之兵，更懷疑貳，遂為陳人所敗。

translations.literal: But the troops under Hua Jiao's command further harbored doubts and divided loyalties; thereupon they were defeated by the men of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Hua Jiao's own troops wavered in loyalty and were beaten by Chen.

sentences.zh: 皎得脫身歸梁。

translations.literal: Jiao was able to slip away and return to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao alone escaped and fled back to Liang.

sentences.zh: 定旣孤軍懸隔，進退路絕，陳人乘勝，水陸逼之。

translations.literal: Ding had already become an isolated army cut off afar; advance and retreat were severed; the men of Chen, riding victory, pressed him by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was now an isolated force cut off far from support with no line of retreat; Chen pressed their advantage by land and water.

sentences.zh: 定乃率所部斫竹開路，且行且戰，欲趣湘州，而湘州已陷。

translations.literal: Ding thereupon led his division, hewing bamboo to open a path, fighting as he marched, intending to hurry toward Xiang Province — but Xiang Province had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Ding led his men forward, cutting bamboo to blaze a trail and fighting all the way toward Xiang Province — only to learn that Xiang Province had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 徐度等知定窮迫，遣使偽與定通和，重為盟誓，許放還國。

translations.literal: Xu Du and the others, knowing Ding was driven to extremity, sent envoys falsely to treat with Ding, solemnly renewing oaths of alliance and promising to let him return home.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Ding was cornered, Xu Du and the others sent envoys offering a sham peace, swearing fresh oaths and promising safe passage home.

sentences.zh: 定疑其詭詐，欲力戰死之。

translations.literal: Ding suspected their treacherous deceit and wished to fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Ding suspected a trap and wanted to die fighting.

sentences.zh: 而定長史〔長〕孫隆及諸將等多勸定和，定乃許之。

translations.literal: But Ding's chief administrator 〔Cháng〕sun Long and the other commanders repeatedly urged Ding to accept peace; Ding thereupon consented.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his chief administrator Changsun Long and the other officers urged peace again and again, and at last Ding agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是與度等刑牲歃血，解仗就船。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Du and the others they slaughtered a victim and drank the blood of the oath, laid down arms, and boarded the boats.
translations.idiomatic: He then swore blood-oath with Xu Du and the rest, laid down his weapons, and went aboard their boats.

sentences.zh: 遂為度等所執，〔所部〕衆軍亦被囚虜，送詣丹陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon they were seized by Du and the others; 〔his〕 subordinate troops were also captured and imprisoned, and sent to Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: They were seized at once; his troops were taken prisoner as well and marched to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 居數月，憂憤發病卒。

translations.literal: After several months, grief and rage brought on illness and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Within months, grief and rage brought on illness and he died.

sentences.zh: 子樂嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yue succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yue succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 楊摽字顯進，正平高涼人也。

translations.literal: Yang Biao, styled Xianjin, was a native of Gaoliang in Zhengping.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao, courtesy name Xianjin, came from Gaoliang in Zhengping commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖貴、父猛，並為縣令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gui and his father Meng were both county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gui and his father Meng had both served as county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 摽少豪俠有志氣。

translations.literal: Biao in youth was bold and chivalrous and had high spirit.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Biao was bold, chivalrous, and full of resolve.

sentences.zh: 魏孝昌中，爾朱榮殺害朝士，大司馬、城陽王元徽逃難投摽，摽藏而免之。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era, Erzhu Rong killed court gentlemen; the Grand Marshal, Prince of Chengyang Yuan Hui, fled in distress and sought refuge with Biao; Biao hid him and saved him.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiaochang, when Erzhu Rong slaughtered court officials, Grand Marshal Yuan Hui, Prince of Chengyang, fled to Biao for refuge; Biao concealed him and kept him alive.

sentences.zh: 孝莊帝立，徽乃出，復為司州牧。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang was enthroned, Hui thereupon came forth and again became Governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, Hui emerged from hiding and again became governor of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 由是摽以義烈聞。

translations.literal: From this Biao became known for righteous valor.
translations.idiomatic: From that act Biao won renown for righteous courage.

sentences.zh: 擢拜伏波將軍、給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed General Who Subdues the Waves and Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who subdues the waves and attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，孝莊欲往晉陽就爾朱榮，詔摽率其宗人收船馬渚。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Emperor Xiaozhuang wished to go to Jinyang to join Erzhu Rong; an edict ordered Biao to lead his clansmen to gather boats at Mazhu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Emperor Xiaozhuang meant to withdraw to Jinyang and join Erzhu Rong; an edict ordered Biao to rally his kinsmen and collect boats at Mazhu.

sentences.zh: 摽未至，帝已北度太行，摽遂匿所收船，不以資敵。

translations.literal: Before Biao arrived, the Emperor had already crossed the Taihang northward; Biao thereupon hid the boats he had gathered and did not supply the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Before Biao arrived the emperor had already crossed the Taihang northward; Biao hid the boats he had gathered rather than let them fall to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 及爾朱榮奉帝南討，至馬渚，摽乃具船以濟王師。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong escorted the Emperor south to campaign, and reached Mazhu, Biao thereupon prepared boats to ferry the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong escorted the emperor south to campaign and reached Mazhu, Biao furnished boats to ferry the imperial army across.

sentences.zh: 顥平，封肥如五百戶，加鎮遠將軍、步兵校尉，行濟北郡事。

translations.literal: When Hao was pacified, Biao was enfeoffed with five hundred households at Feiru, with the added titles General Who Pacifies the Distant and Commandant of Footsoldiers, acting Administrator of Jibei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Hao was defeated, Biao received a fief of five hundred households at Feiru, the added titles general who pacifies the distant and commandant of footsoldiers, and acting charge of Jibei commandery.

sentences.zh: 進都督、平東將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: He was advanced to area commander, General Who Pacifies the East, and Grand Master of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to area commander, general who pacifies the east, and grand master of palace attendance.

sentences.zh: 從魏孝武入關，進爵為侯，增邑八百戶，加撫軍、銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei in entering the Pass; he was advanced in rank to marquis with eight hundred additional households, and given the added titles General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xiaowu through the Pass into Guanzhong, was raised to marquis with eight hundred additional households, and given the added ranks of general who pacifies the army and grand master with the silver seal and blue ribbon.

sentences.zh: 時東魏遷鄴，太祖欲知其所為，乃遣摽間行詣鄴以觀察之。

translations.literal: At the time Eastern Wei moved the capital to Ye; the Grand Progenitor wished to know what they were doing and thereupon sent Biao by secret route to Ye to observe.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei moved its capital to Ye, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai wanted to know what they were up to and sent Biao by secret route to Ye to reconnoiter.

sentences.zh: 使還，稱旨，授通直散騎常侍、車騎將軍。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, it matched the intent; he was appointed Direct Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His report satisfied the throne, and he was made direct regular attendant of scattered cavalry and general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 稽胡恃險不賓，屢行抄竊，以摽兼黃門侍郎，往慰撫之。

translations.literal: The Ji-hu relied on the passes and would not submit; they repeatedly raided and plundered; Biao was concurrently made Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and sent to comfort and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji-hu held the mountain passes and refused submission, raiding again and again; Biao was given concurrent appointment as gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gate and sent to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 摽頗有權略，能得邊情，誘化酋渠，多來款附，乃有隨摽入朝者。

translations.literal: Biao had considerable resource in stratagem and could grasp border conditions; he won over and converted tribal chiefs, and many came to submit in good faith; there were even those who followed Biao to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Biao was shrewd in frontier affairs; he won over tribal chiefs until many submitted, and some even followed him to court.

sentences.zh: 時弘農為東魏守，摽從太祖攻拔之。

translations.literal: At the time Hongnong was held by Eastern Wei; Biao followed the Grand Progenitor in attacking and capturing it.
translations.idiomatic: Hongnong was then held by Eastern Wei; Biao marched with Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai and helped take it.

sentences.zh: 然自河以北，猶附東魏。

translations.literal: Yet from the Yellow River northward, many still adhered to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yet north of the Yellow River many districts still sided with Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 摽父猛先為邵郡白水令，摽與其豪右相知，請微行詣邵郡，舉兵以應朝廷。

translations.literal: Biao's father Meng had earlier been magistrate of Baishui in Shao commandery; Biao was acquainted with its local magnates; he requested to go in plain dress to Shao commandery and raise troops to respond to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Biao's father Meng had once been magistrate of Baishui in Shao commandery; knowing the local magnates there, Biao asked leave to go in disguise to Shao and raise troops for the court.

sentences.zh: 太祖許之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 摽遂行，與土豪王覆憐等陰謀舉事，密相應會者三千人，內外俱發，遂拔邵郡。

translations.literal: Biao thereupon set out; with the local strongman Wang Fuling and others he plotted rebellion in secret; those secretly agreeing to join inside and outside numbered three thousand; both within and without rose together, and thereupon captured Shao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Biao set out and, with the local magnate Wang Fuling and others, plotted in secret; three thousand men pledged themselves inside and out, and when all rose together they took Shao commandery.

sentences.zh: 擒郡守程保及令四人，並斬之。

translations.literal: They captured the commandery administrator Cheng Bao and four magistrates, and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: They captured commandery administrator Cheng Bao and four county magistrates and beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 衆議推摽行郡事，摽以因覆憐成事，遂表覆憐為邵郡守。

translations.literal: The assembly wished to put Biao in charge of commandery affairs; Biao, holding that success had come through Fuling, thereupon memorialized Fuling as Administrator of Shao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The local leaders wanted Biao to run the commandery, but he insisted the victory belonged to Wang Fuling and memorialized Fuling as administrator of Shao commandery.

sentences.zh: 以功授大行臺左丞，率義徒更為經略。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Left Assistant of the Great Mobile Headquarters and led the loyalist bands in further planning and operations.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made left assistant of the great mobile headquarters and led the loyalist bands in further frontier operations.

sentences.zh: 於是遣諜人誘說東魏城堡，旬月之間，正平、河北、南

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent spies to entice Eastern Wei fortresses; within ten days and a month, Zhengping, Hebei, South
translations.idiomatic: He then sent agents to win over Eastern Wei strongholds; within a month or so, Zhengping, Hebei, South

translations.literal: (Shè) [emended: Fén]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Fén]

sentences.zh: 〔汾〕、二絳、建州、

translations.literal: 〔Fén〕, the Two Jiangs, Jian Province,
translations.idiomatic: Fen, the Two Jiangs, Jian Province,

translations.literal: (Dà) [emended: Tài]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Tài]

sentences.zh: 〔太〕寧等城，並有請為內應者，大軍因攻而拔之。

translations.literal: 〔Tài〕 Ning and other cities all had men seeking to serve as inside collaborators; the great army thereupon attacked and took them.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Ning, and other cities as well, all had men offering to serve as inside contacts; the main force then attacked and took them.

sentences.zh: 以摽行正平郡事，左丞如故。

translations.literal: Biao was made acting Administrator of Zhengping commandery; his left assistant post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Biao was given acting charge of Zhengping commandery while keeping his left assistant post.

sentences.zh: 齊神武敗于沙苑，其將韓軌、潘洛、可朱渾元等為殿，摽分兵要截，殺傷甚衆。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan was defeated at Shaye, his commanders Han Gui, Pan Luo, Kezhuhun Yuan, and others served as rearguard; Biao divided his forces to intercept at critical points and killed and wounded very many.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan was beaten at Shaye, his generals Han Gui, Pan Luo, Kezhuhun Yuan, and others covered the retreat; Biao split his force to cut them off and killed or wounded a great many.

sentences.zh: 東雍州刺史馬恭懼摽威聲，棄城遁走。

translations.literal: Eastern Yong Province Inspector Ma Gong, fearing Biao's martial renown, abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gong, Eastern Wei inspector of Eastern Yong Province, feared Biao's reputation, abandoned his post, and fled.

sentences.zh: 摽遂移據東雍州。

translations.literal: Biao thereupon shifted his base to occupy Eastern Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Biao then moved his headquarters and took control of Eastern Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 太祖以摽有謀略，堪委邊任，乃表行建州事。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor, because Biao had strategic counsel and was fit to be entrusted with frontier duty, thereupon memorialized him to act as governor of Jian Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, judging Biao shrewd and fit for frontier command, recommended him to act as governor of Jian Province.

sentences.zh: 時建州遠在敵境三百餘裏，然摽威恩夙著，所經之處，多並贏糧附之。

translations.literal: At the time Jian Province lay more than three hundred li deep in enemy territory, yet Biao's martial prestige and gracious rule had long been renowned; wherever he passed, many brought grain on their backs to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Province lay more than three hundred li inside enemy country, yet Biao's authority and kindness were already famed; wherever he marched, people came carrying grain to join him.

sentences.zh: 比至建州，衆已一萬。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Jian Province, his followers already numbered ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Jian Province his force already numbered ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 東魏刺史車折于洛出兵逆戰，摽擊敗之。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Governor Chezhe Yuluo led troops out to meet him in battle; Biao defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei governor Chezhe Yuluo marched out to fight him; Biao routed him.

sentences.zh: 又破其行臺斛律俱步騎二萬於州西，大獲甲仗及軍資，以給義士。

translations.literal: He also routed Mobile Headquarters Director Hulu Ju's twenty thousand infantry and cavalry west of the province, taking great quantities of armor, weapons, and military supplies, which he used to equip the loyalist fighters.
translations.idiomatic: He also smashed mobile headquarters director Hulu Ju's twenty thousand foot and horse west of the province, seizing large stores of arms and supplies for his loyalist troops.

sentences.zh: 由是威名大振。

translations.literal: From this his martial renown greatly swelled.
translations.idiomatic: His fame as a commander rose sharply from that victory.

sentences.zh: 東魏遣太保侯景攻陷正平，復遣行臺薛循義率兵與斛律俱相會，於是敵衆漸盛。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei sent Grand Guardian Hou Jing to attack and take Zhengping, and again sent Mobile Headquarters Director Xue Xunyi with troops to join Hulu Ju; thus the enemy forces gradually grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent Grand Guardian Hou Jing to retake Zhengping and dispatched mobile headquarters director Xue Xunyi to join Hulu Ju, and enemy strength steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 摽以孤軍無援，且腹背受敵，謀欲拔還。

translations.literal: Biao, being an isolated army without reinforcements and attacked from both front and rear, planned to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off, unsupported, and pressed from front and rear, Biao planned to pull back.

sentences.zh: 恐義徒背叛，遂偽為太祖書，遣人若從外送來者，云已遣軍四道赴援。

translations.literal: Fearing the loyalist bands would turn traitor, he thereupon forged a letter from the Grand Progenitor and sent a man as though delivering it from outside, saying armies had already been dispatched on four routes to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing his loyalist bands might desert him, he forged a letter from Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai and had a messenger deliver it as if from outside, claiming relief columns were already marching on four routes.

sentences.zh: 因令人漏泄，使所在知之。

translations.literal: He then had men leak the news so that those in the region would learn of it.
translations.idiomatic: He then deliberately leaked the report so the countryside would hear it.

sentences.zh: 又分土人義首，令領所部四出抄掠，擬供軍費。

translations.literal: He also divided up the local loyalist chieftains and had them lead their bands out in all directions to raid and plunder, intending to supply army expenses.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent local loyalist leaders out in every direction with their men to raid for supplies.

sentences.zh: 摽分遣訖，遂於夜中拔還邵郡。

translations.literal: When Biao had finished assigning them, he thereupon withdrew by night back to Shao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Once those detachments were dispatched, he withdrew by night to Shao commandery.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉其權以全軍，卽授建州刺史。

translations.literal: The court praised his resourcefulness in preserving the army and at once appointed him Governor of Jian Province.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his shrewdness in saving his army and at once made him governor of Jian Province.

sentences.zh: 時東魏以正平為東雍州，遣薛榮祖鎮之。

translations.literal: At the time Eastern Wei made Zhengping into Eastern Yong Province and sent Xue Rongzu to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei had reorganized Zhengping as Eastern Yong Province and posted Xue Rongzu there.

sentences.zh: 摽將謀取之，乃先遣奇兵，急攻汾橋。

translations.literal: Biao planned to take it; he first sent surprise troops to attack Fen Bridge urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Biao meant to retake it and first sent a strike force against Fen Bridge.

sentences.zh: 榮祖果盡出城中戰士，於汾橋拒守。

translations.literal: Rongzu indeed sent out all the city warriors to hold the Fen Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu emptied the city and threw every fighter he had into holding Fen Bridge.

sentences.zh: 其夜，摽率步騎二千，從他道濟，遂襲克之。

translations.literal: That night Biao led two thousand infantry and cavalry by another route across the river and thereupon stormed and took the city.
translations.idiomatic: That night Biao led two thousand foot and horse by another crossing, stormed the city, and took it.

sentences.zh: 進驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 旣而邵郡民以郡東叛，郡守郭武安脫身走免。

translations.literal: Before long the people of Shao commandery rebelled in the east of the commandery; commandery administrator Guo Wu'an slipped away and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the eastern part of Shao commandery rebelled; administrator Guo Wu'an escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 摽又率兵攻而復之。

translations.literal: Biao again led troops to attack and recover it.
translations.idiomatic: Biao marched again, retook the district, and restored order.

sentences.zh: 轉正平郡守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Zhengping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administrator of Zhengping commandery.

sentences.zh: 又擊破東魏南絳郡，虜其郡守屈僧珍。

translations.literal: He also routed Eastern Wei's Southern Jiang commandery and captured its administrator Qu Sengzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated Eastern Wei's Southern Jiang commandery and captured its administrator Qu Sengzhen.

sentences.zh: 錄前後功，別封郃陽縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Recording his successive merits, he was separately enfeoffed Baron of Heyang county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his accumulated service he received a separate enfeoffment as baron of Heyang with five hundred fief households.

sentences.zh: 邙山之戰，摽攻拔柏穀塢，因卽鎮之。

translations.literal: At the battle of Mount Mang, Biao attacked and took Baigu Stockade and thereupon garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Mang he stormed Baigu Stockade and garrisoned it.

sentences.zh: 及大軍不利，摽亦拔還。

translations.literal: When the great army met misfortune, Biao also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force was routed, Biao pulled back as well.

sentences.zh: 而東魏將侯景率騎追摽，摽與儀同韋法保同心抗禦，且前經十數里，景乃引退。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei general Hou Jing led cavalry in pursuit of Biao; Biao and Attendant-in-Regular Wei Fabao with one heart resisted him, and after advancing more than ten li, Jing thereupon drew back.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei general Hou Jing pursued him with cavalry; Biao and Wei Fabao stood together and fought him off, and after more than ten li Jing broke off the chase.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，賜帛三百疋。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor commended him and granted three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai praised him and rewarded him with three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 復授建州刺史，鎮車箱。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Governor of Jian Province and garrisoned Chexiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made governor of Jian Province and posted at Chexiang.

sentences.zh: 摽久從軍役，未及葬父，至是表請還葬。

translations.literal: Biao had long been on campaign and had not yet buried his father; at this he memorialized asking to return and bury him.
translations.idiomatic: Biao had spent years in the field without burying his father; he now petitioned to return home for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 詔贈其父車騎大將軍、儀同三司、晉州刺史，贈其母夏陽縣君，並給儀衛。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made his father General of Chariots and Cavalry with Yitong of the Three Precedences and Governor of Jin Province, posthumously made his mother Lady of Xiayang county, and granted ceremonial guards for both.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made his father general of chariots and cavalry with yitong of the Three Precedences and governor of Jin Province, ennobled his mother as lady of Xiayang county, and granted ceremonial guards for the rites.

sentences.zh: 州里榮之。

translations.literal: The province and commandery regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: The whole region took it as a mark of honor.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武圍玉壁，別令侯景趣齊子嶺。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan besieged Yubi, he separately ordered Hou Jing to press toward Qizi Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan besieged Yubi he also ordered Hou Jing to push toward Qizi Ridge.

sentences.zh: 摽恐入寇邵郡，率騎禦之。

translations.literal: Biao feared an incursion into Shao commandery and led cavalry to block him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a raid into Shao commandery, Biao led cavalry to intercept him.

sentences.zh: 景聞摽至，斫木斷路者六十餘裏，猶驚而不安，遂退還河陽，其見憚如此。

translations.literal: When Jing heard Biao had arrived, though his men had felled trees and blocked the road for more than sixty li, he was still alarmed and uneasy, and thereupon withdrew back to Heyang — such was the fear he inspired.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing learned Biao was coming, he had trees cut and the road blocked for more than sixty li, yet he remained uneasy and withdrew to Heyang — such was the dread Biao inspired.

sentences.zh: 十二年，進授大都督，加晉建二州諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was advanced to Grand Area Commander and given military command over Jin and Jian provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was promoted to grand area commander with military authority over Jin and Jian provinces.

sentences.zh: 又攻破蓼塢，獲〔東〕魏將李顯，進儀同三司。

translations.literal: He also attacked and took Liaowu Stockade, captured 〔Dōng〕 Wei general Li Xian, and was advanced to Yitong of the Three Precedences.
translations.idiomatic: He also stormed Liaowu Stockade, captured Eastern Wei general Li Xian, and was raised to yitong of the Three Precedences.

sentences.zh: 尋遷開府，復除建州邵郡河內汲郡黎陽等諸軍事，領邵郡。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Kaifu, again made commander of the military affairs of Jian Province, Shao commandery, Henei, Ji commandery, Liyang, and others, and placed in charge of Shao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to kaifu, given command over the military affairs of Jian Province, Shao commandery, Henei, Ji, Liyang, and neighboring districts, and put in charge of Shao commandery.

sentences.zh: 十六年，大軍東討，授大行臺尚書，率義衆先驅敵境，攻其四戍，拔之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the great army marched east to chastise the enemy; Biao was appointed Great Mobile Headquarters Minister and led loyalist forces as vanguard into enemy territory, attacked four outposts, and took them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, when the main army marched east against Qi, Biao was made great mobile headquarters minister, led loyalist troops into enemy country as vanguard, and captured four border forts.

sentences.zh: 時以齊軍不出，乃追摽還。

translations.literal: At the time, because the Qi army did not come out, they recalled Biao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi army refused battle, the court recalled him.

sentences.zh: 併肥如、合陽二邑，合一千八百戶，改封華陽縣侯。

translations.literal: Combining the two districts of Feiru and Heyang for one thousand eight hundred households, he was given a new enfeoffment as Marquis of Huayang county.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was enlarged by combining Feiru and Heyang for one thousand eight hundred households, and his title was changed to Marquis of Huayang.

sentences.zh: 又於邵郡置邵州，以摽為刺史，率所部兵鎮之。

translations.literal: Shao Province was also established within Shao commandery, with Biao as its governor, leading his own troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Province was created within Shao commandery, with Biao as governor commanding his own troops there.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，遷少師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding he was transferred to Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 4 he was made junior preceptor.

sentences.zh: 其年，大軍圍洛陽，詔摽率義兵萬餘人出軹關。

translations.literal: That same year the great army besieged Luoyang; an edict ordered Biao to lead more than ten thousand loyalist troops out through Zhi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, as the main force besieged Luoyang, an edict ordered Biao to lead more than ten thousand loyalist troops out through Zhi Pass.

sentences.zh: 然摽自鎮東境二十餘年，數與齊人戰，每常克獲，以此遂有輕敵之心。

translations.literal: Yet Biao had garrisoned the eastern frontier for more than twenty years, fighting Qi men repeatedly and winning every time; for this reason he came to hold enemy forces in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Biao had held the eastern frontier for more than twenty years and had beaten Qi again and again; success had bred contempt for the enemy.

sentences.zh: 時洛陽未下，而摽深入敵境，又不設備。

translations.literal: Luoyang had not yet fallen, yet Biao penetrated deep into enemy territory without establishing defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang had not yet fallen, yet he plunged deep into enemy country without taking precautions.

sentences.zh: 齊人奄至，大破摽軍。

translations.literal: Qi forces came suddenly and routed Biao's army.
translations.idiomatic: Qi troops fell on him suddenly and shattered his army.

sentences.zh: 摽以衆敗，遂降于齊。

translations.literal: Biao, his force having been defeated, thereupon surrendered to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: With his force broken, Biao surrendered to Qi.

sentences.zh: 摽之立勳也，有慷慨壯烈之志，及軍敗，遂就虜以求苟免。

translations.literal: When Biao had first won merit he had possessed a generous and heroic will; when his army was defeated he then sought survival by going over to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The man who had once won fame for bold service now, once beaten, chose submission to save his life.

sentences.zh: 時論以此鄙之。

translations.literal: Opinion of the time held him in contempt for this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 朝廷猶錄其功，不以為罪，令其子襲爵。

translations.literal: The court still recorded his past merits and did not treat it as a crime, letting his son inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: The court still honored his earlier service, did not treat the surrender as a crime, and allowed his son to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 摽之敗也，新平郡守韓盛亦於洛陽戰沒。

translations.literal: When Biao was defeated, Xingping commandery administrator Han Sheng also fell in battle at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao fell, Xingping commandery administrator Han Sheng also died fighting at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 盛字文熾，南陽

translations.literal: Sheng, styled Wenchì, was a native of Nanyang
translations.idiomatic: Han Sheng, courtesy name Wenchì, came from Nanyang in

translations.literal: (Zhǔ) [emended: Dǔ]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Dǔ]

sentences.zh: 〔堵〕陽人也。

translations.literal: 〔Dǔ〕 Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yang commandery.

sentences.zh: 五世祖遠，為鄭縣令，因徙居京兆之渭南焉。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Yuan was magistrate of Zheng county and for that reason moved to reside at Weinan in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Yuan had served as magistrate of Zheng county and moved the family to Weinan in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖良，舉秀才，奉朝請、姑臧令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Liang passed the provincial examination, became a palace attendant, and was magistrate of Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Liang had passed the provincial examination, entered service as a palace attendant, and become magistrate of Guzang.

sentences.zh: 祖與，魏儻城郡守，贈直州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu was Eastern Wei Administrator of Tangcheng commandery; posthumously made Governor of Zhi Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu had been Eastern Wei administrator of Tangcheng commandery and was posthumously made governor of Zhi Province.

sentences.zh: 父先藻，安夷鄜城二郡守，贈鎮遠將軍、義州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xianzao was administrator of Anyi and Fucheng commanderies; posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Distant and Governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xianzao had governed Anyi and Fucheng commanderies and was posthumously made general who pacifies the distant and governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 盛幼有操行，涉獵經史，兼善騎射，膂力過人。

translations.literal: Sheng from youth had proper conduct, ranged through the classics and histories, and was skilled at both horsemanship and archery; his physical strength surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Sheng was upright in conduct, well read in the classics and histories, and skilled in horsemanship and archery; his strength was extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 魏大統初，起家開府行參軍。

translations.literal: Early in Eastern Wei Great Unity he began his career as acting staff officer of the Kaifu office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Great Unity era he entered service as acting staff officer in a kaifu headquarters.

sentences.zh: 轉參軍事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made staff officer.

sentences.zh: 從李遠積年征討，每有戰功。

translations.literal: He followed Li Yuan on campaigns for many years and every time won battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned under Li Yuan for many years and won merit in every fight.

sentences.zh: 累遷至都督、輔國將軍、中散大夫、帥都督、持節、平東將軍、太中大夫、銀青光祿大夫、大都督。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to area commander, General Who Assists the State, Palace Attendant Gentleman, Chief Area Commander, Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of Palace Attendance, Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon, and Grand Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to area commander, general who assists the state, palace attendant gentleman, chief area commander, bearer of the staff, general who pacifies the east, grand master of palace attendance, grand master with the silver seal and blue ribbon, and grand area commander.

sentences.zh: 明帝二年，封臨湍縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Ming he was enfeoffed Viscount of Lintuan county with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Ming he was enfeoffed Viscount of Lintuan with three hundred fief households.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，授使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、虞部下大夫，出為新平郡守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding he was given the staff, made General of Chariots and Cavalry with Yitong of the Three Precedences and Senior Master of the Yu Department, and sent out as Administrator of Xingping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 4 he received bearer of the staff, was made general of chariots and cavalry with yitong of the Three Precedences and senior master of the Yu Department, and sent out as administrator of Xingping commandery.

sentences.zh: 居官清靜，嚴而不殘，矜恤孤貧，抑挫豪右，賊盜止息，郡治肅然。

translations.literal: In office he was quiet and pure, strict without cruelty, compassionate to orphans and the poor, and curbed the great families; bandits and robbers ceased, and the commandery was governed with order.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was calm and fair, strict but not harsh, tender toward orphans and the poor, and firm against the powerful; banditry ceased and the commandery was governed in good order.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官從晉公護東討，於洛陽戰沒。

translations.literal: Soon, in his existing office, he followed Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu on the eastern campaign and fell in battle at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he marched east under Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu and fell fighting at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 贈淅洛義三州刺史，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Governor of the three provinces of Xi, Luo, and Yi; his posthumous name was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made governor of Xi, Luo, and Yi provinces and given the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子謙嗣。

translations.literal: His son Qian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 官至大都督。

translations.literal: He rose to Grand Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Qian rose to grand area commander.

sentences.zh: 盛二兄，德輿、仲恭。

translations.literal: Sheng had two elder brothers, Deyu and Zhonggong.
translations.idiomatic: Two elder brothers preceded him: Deyu and Zhonggong.

sentences.zh: 德輿姿貌魁傑，有異常人。

translations.literal: Deyu had a towering appearance unlike ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu was imposing in stature and unlike ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 歷官持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、通洛慈澗防主、邵州刺史、任城縣男。

translations.literal: His offices in succession included Bearer of the Staff, General of Chariots and Cavalry with Yitong of the Three Precedences, Commander of the Tongluo-Cijian Defense Line, Governor of Shao Province, and Baron of Rencheng county.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as bearer of the staff, general of chariots and cavalry with yitong of the Three Precedences, commander of the Tongluo-Cijian defense line, governor of Shao Province, and baron of Rencheng county.

sentences.zh: 仲恭美容儀，澹於榮利。

translations.literal: Zhonggong had fine looks and was indifferent to glory and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonggong was handsome and cared little for rank or gain.

sentences.zh: 郡累辟為功曹、中正。

translations.literal: The commandery repeatedly summoned him as merit officer and chief rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery repeatedly tried to appoint him merit officer and chief rectifier.

sentences.zh: 仲恭答曰：「第五之號，豈減驃騎乎！

translations.literal: Zhonggong replied: "Is the title of Fifth Rank any less than General of Agile Cavalry!
translations.idiomatic: Zhonggong answered, "Is a fifth-rank post any less than general of agile cavalry?

sentences.zh: 」後歷廣原、靈原、新豐三縣令，所在皆有聲績。

translations.literal: " Later he served in succession as magistrate of Guangyuan, Lingyuan, and Xinfeng counties; wherever he went he left a record of reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he served in turn as magistrate of Guangyuan, Lingyuan, and Xinfeng, and everywhere he went left a record of good repute.

sentences.zh: 有八子，並有志操。

translations.literal: He had eight sons, all with purposeful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons, all men of principle.

sentences.zh: 少子紉約，後最知名。

translations.literal: The youngest son Renyue later became the best known.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest, Renyue, later became the best known.

sentences.zh: 裴寬字長寬，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Kuan, styled Changkuan, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kuan, courtesy name Changkuan, came from Wenxi in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖德歡，魏中書郎、河內郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dehuan was Eastern Wei Secretariat Gentleman and Administrator of Henei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dehuan had served Eastern Wei as secretariat gentleman and administrator of Henei commandery.

sentences.zh: 父靜慮，銀青光祿大夫，贈汾州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Jinglü was Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon; posthumously made Governor of Fen Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jinglü had been grand master with the silver seal and blue ribbon and was posthumously made governor of Fen Province.

sentences.zh: 寬儀貌瑰偉，博涉羣書，弱冠為州里所稱。

translations.literal: Kuan had a magnificent bearing, ranged broadly through books, and before coming of age was acclaimed in his province and commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan was striking in appearance, widely read, and acclaimed locally before he came of age.

sentences.zh: 與二弟漢、尼是和知名。

translations.literal: Together with his two younger brothers Han and Ni he shared a reputation for harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brothers Han and Ni were known together for their close harmony.

sentences.zh: 親歿，撫弟以篤友聞。

translations.literal: When their parents died he raised his brothers and was known for devoted friendship.
translations.idiomatic: After their parents died he raised his brothers and was famed for devoted brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 滎陽鄭孝穆常謂從弟文直曰：「裴長寬兄弟，天倫篤睦，人之師表。

translations.literal: Xingyang Zheng Xiaomu often told his cousin Wenzhi: "Pei Changkuan and his brothers are deeply harmonious in family bonds — a model for others.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xiaomu of Xingyang often told his cousin Wenzhi, "Pei Changkuan and his brothers are models of family devotion.

sentences.zh: 吾愛之重之。

translations.literal: I love and esteem them.
translations.idiomatic: I love and respect them.

sentences.zh: 汝可與之遊處。

translations.literal: You should associate and spend time with them."
translations.idiomatic: You should keep company with them."

sentences.zh: 」年十三，以選為魏孝明帝挽郎，釋褐員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: " At age thirteen, by selection he became a mourning attendant for Emperor Xiaoming of Wei; at first appointment he was made assistant gentleman attendant at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he was chosen as a mourning attendant for Emperor Xiaoming of Wei and, on entering office, was made assistant gentleman attendant at leisure.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武末，除廣陵王府直兵參軍，加寧朔將軍、員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei's reign, he was appointed direct military adjutant of the Prince of Guangling's household, with the added ranks of general who calms the north and assistant attendant-in-ordinary at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei's reign he was made direct military adjutant of the Prince of Guangling's household, with the added titles of general who calms the north and assistant attendant-in-ordinary at leisure.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，寬謂其諸弟曰：「權臣擅命，乘輿播越，戰爭方始，當何所依？

translations.literal: When Xiaowu moved west, Kuan said to his younger brothers: "A powerful minister usurps authority, the imperial carriage is driven to exile, and war is just beginning — where should we rely?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Kuan asked his younger brothers, "A powerful minister has seized command, the emperor has been driven into exile, and war is just beginning — where can we turn?

sentences.zh: 」諸弟咸不能對。

translations.literal: " All the younger brothers were unable to answer.
translations.idiomatic: None of his brothers could answer.

sentences.zh: 寬曰：「君臣逆順，大義昭然。

translations.literal: Kuan said: "The right and wrong between ruler and subject — the great principle is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan said, "The right and wrong between ruler and subject is plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 今天子西幸，理無東面，以虧臣節。

translations.literal: Now that the Son of Heaven has gone west, by principle we cannot turn east and thereby fail in our duty as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has gone west; by principle we cannot turn east and betray our duty as subjects.

sentences.zh: 」乃將家屬避難於大石岩。

translations.literal: " He then took his family and sought refuge at Great Stone Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: He then took his family and sought refuge at Great Stone Cliff.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信鎮洛陽，始出見焉。

translations.literal: When Dugu Xin was stationed at Luoyang, he first went out to see him.
translations.idiomatic: When Dugu Xin was stationed at Luoyang, Kuan went out to see him.

sentences.zh: 時汾州刺史韋子粲降於東魏，子粲兄弟在關中者，咸已從坐。

translations.literal: At the time Fen Prefecture inspector Wei Zican had surrendered to Eastern Wei, and Zican's brothers who were in Guanzhong had all been implicated and punished.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fen Prefecture inspector Wei Zican had surrendered to Eastern Wei, and Zican's brothers in Guanzhong had all been punished as accomplices.

sentences.zh: 其季弟子爽先在洛，窘急，乃投寬。

translations.literal: His youngest brother's son Shuang was already in Luoyang; in distress and urgency, he fled to Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zican's youngest brother's son Shuang was already in Luoyang; desperate, he fled to Kuan.

sentences.zh: 寬開懷納之。

translations.literal: Kuan opened his heart and received him.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan welcomed him without reservation.

sentences.zh: 遇有大赦，或傳子爽合免，因爾遂出。

translations.literal: There happened to be a great amnesty, and some said Shuang ought to be pardoned; on that account he then went out.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed, and word spread that Shuang would be spared; on that basis he left.

sentences.zh: 子爽卒以伏法。

translations.literal: Shuang in the end was executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang was executed in the end.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信召而責之。

translations.literal: Dugu Xin summoned and rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin summoned Kuan and rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 寬曰：「窮來見歸，義無執送。

translations.literal: Kuan said: "When someone in distress comes seeking refuge, by right one does not seize and hand him over.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan said, "When someone in distress comes seeking refuge, it would be wrong to seize him and turn him in.

sentences.zh: 今日獲罪，是所甘心。

translations.literal: If today I receive punishment, that is what I willingly accept.
translations.idiomatic: If I am punished for it today, I accept that willingly.

sentences.zh: 」以經赦宥，遂得不坐。

translations.literal: " Because he had passed through an amnesty pardon, he was in the end not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Because the case fell under the amnesty, he was not punished after all.

sentences.zh: 大統五年，授都督、同軌防長史，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Datong, he was appointed area commander and chief of staff of Tonggui Defense, with the added rank of general who captures enemies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Datong he was made area commander and chief of staff of Tonggui Defense, with the added rank of general who captures enemies.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從防主韋法保向潁川，解侯景圍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he followed the defense commander Wei Fabao toward Yingchuan and lifted Hou Jing's siege.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he followed defense commander Wei Fabao to Yingchuan and lifted Hou Jing's siege.

sentences.zh: 景密圖南叛，軍中頗有知者。

translations.literal: Jing secretly plotted to rebel southward, and in the army quite a few knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was secretly plotting to rebel southward, and many in the army knew it.

sentences.zh: 以其事計未成，外示無貳，往來諸軍間，侍從寡少。

translations.literal: Because his plan had not yet succeeded, outwardly he showed no disloyalty; he moved among the various armies, and his attendants were few.
translations.idiomatic: Because his plan was not yet ripe, he outwardly showed no disloyalty, moved among the various armies, and kept few attendants.

sentences.zh: 軍中名將，必躬自造，至於法保，尤被親附。

translations.literal: Famous generals in the army — he always went in person to visit them; as for Fabao, he was especially treated with intimacy and attachment.
translations.idiomatic: He always visited the army's famous generals in person; Fabao in particular he cultivated with special intimacy.

sentences.zh: 寬謂法保曰：「侯景狡猾，必不肯入關。

translations.literal: Kuan said to Fabao: "Hou Jing is crafty; he will surely not enter the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan told Fabao, "Hou Jing is crafty and will surely not enter the passes.

sentences.zh: 雖托款於公，恐未可信。

translations.literal: Although he pledges goodwill to you, I fear he is not yet to be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Though he pledges goodwill to you, I fear he cannot yet be trusted.

sentences.zh: 若仗兵以斬之，亦一時之計也。

translations.literal: If you rely on troops to behead him, that too is a plan for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: If you use troops to kill him, that would be one immediate option.

sentences.zh: 如曰不然，便須深加嚴警，不得信其誑誘，自貽後悔。

translations.literal: If you say otherwise, then you must deeply strengthen warnings and guards, and must not trust his deceitful enticements and bring regret upon yourself.
translations.idiomatic: If not, you must tighten your guard and not trust his deceitful blandishments, lest you regret it later.

sentences.zh: 」法保納之，然不能圖景，但自固而已。

translations.literal: " Fabao accepted this, yet could not plot against Jing and only fortified himself, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Fabao accepted the advice but could not move against Jing and could only strengthen his own defenses.

sentences.zh: 十四年，與東魏將彭樂、〔樂〕恂戰於新城，因傷被擒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he fought Eastern Wei generals Peng Le and 〔Le〕 Xun at Xincheng and, wounded, was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he fought Eastern Wei generals Peng Le and Xun at Xincheng and, wounded, was captured.

sentences.zh: 至河陰，見齊文襄。

translations.literal: Reaching Heyin, he saw Qi Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At Heyin he was brought before Gao Cheng, Wenxiang of Qi.

sentences.zh: 寬舉止詳雅，善於占對，文襄甚賞異之。

translations.literal: Kuan's bearing was detailed and refined, and he was skilled at measured replies; Wenxiang greatly admired and marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan's bearing was calm and refined, and he answered with poise; Gao Cheng admired him greatly.

sentences.zh: 謂寬曰：「卿三河冠蓋，材識如此，我必使卿富貴。

translations.literal: He said to Kuan: "You are from the eminent families of Sanhe, with talent and insight such as this — I shall surely make you rich and honored.
translations.idiomatic: He told Kuan, "You come from the great families of Sanhe and have talent like this — I will surely make you rich and honored.

sentences.zh: 關中貧

translations.literal: Guanzhong is poor
translations.idiomatic: The Guanzhong region is impoverished

translations.literal: (校) [collated emendation]
translations.idiomatic: [collated emendation]

sentences.zh: 〔狹〕，何足可依，勿懷異圖也。

translations.literal: 〔narrow〕 — what is there worth relying on? Do not harbor other plans.
translations.idiomatic: and narrow — what is there to rely on? Do not harbor other plans.

sentences.zh: 」因解鎖付館，厚加其禮。

translations.literal: " He then removed his fetters and lodged him in a guest house, treating him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He then removed Kuan's fetters, lodged him as a guest, and treated him with great courtesy.

sentences.zh: 寬乃裁臥氊，夜縋而出，因得遁還，見於太祖。

translations.literal: Kuan then cut a sleeping mat, and at night lowered himself by rope and got out; thus he escaped back and was received by the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan cut up a sleeping mat, lowered himself by rope at night, escaped back, and was received by Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 太祖顧謂諸公曰：「被堅執銳，或有其人，疾風勁草，歲寒方驗。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor turned and said to the assembled lords: "Bearing armor and wielding sharp weapons — there may be men for that; strong wind and tough grass — only in the cold year is it tested.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai turned to the assembled lords and said, "There may be men who bear armor and wield sharp weapons, but strong wind and tough grass are tested only in the cold of winter.

sentences.zh: 裴長寬為高澄如此厚遇，乃能冒死歸我。

translations.literal: Pei Changkuan received such generous treatment from Gao Cheng, yet was able to risk death and return to me.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Changkuan was treated so generously by Gao Cheng, yet risked death to return to me.

sentences.zh: 雖古之竹帛所載，何以加之！

translations.literal: Even what the bamboo slips and silk of antiquity record — how could one add to this!
translations.idiomatic: Even the heroes recorded in the annals of antiquity could hardly surpass this!

sentences.zh: 」乃手書署寬名下，授持節、帥都督，封夏陽縣男，邑三百戶，幷賜馬一疋、衣一襲，卽除孔城城主。

translations.literal: " He then wrote by hand under Kuan's name, appointing him bearer of the staff, commander-in-chief, Baron of Xiayang county with a fief of three hundred households, and also bestowing one horse and one suit of clothes; he was at once appointed fortress master of Kongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote Kuan's appointment in his own hand, making him bearer of the staff and commander-in-chief, Baron of Xiayang with a fief of three hundred households, and also gave him a horse and a suit of clothes; Kuan was at once made fortress master of Kongcheng.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，出為

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding, he was sent out as
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoding he was sent out as

translations.literal: (Fen) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Mian]

sentences.zh: 〔沔〕州刺史。

translations.literal: 〔Mian〕 Prefecture inspector.
translations.idiomatic: governor of Mian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋轉魯山防主。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to commander of Lushan Defense.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commander of the Lushan garrison.

sentences.zh: 四年，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was given the added ranks of senior grand general and opening-office status equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was given the added titles of senior grand general and opening-office status equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，行復州事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, he acted as administrator of Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhe he acted as administrator of Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年，除溫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was appointed governor of Wen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed governor of Wen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初陳氏與國通和，每脩聘好。

translations.literal: At first Chen and our state were on friendly terms, and each year they maintained diplomatic courtesies.
translations.idiomatic: At first Chen and Zhou maintained friendly relations and exchanged diplomatic courtesies every year.

sentences.zh: 自華皎附後，乃圖寇掠。

translations.literal: After Hua Jiao submitted, they then plotted raids and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: After Hua Jiao defected to Zhou, Chen turned to raiding and plunder.

sentences.zh: 沔州旣接敵境，事資守備，於是復以寬為沔州刺史。

translations.literal: Mian Prefecture bordered the enemy frontier and required defense; therefore Kuan was again made governor of Mian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mian Prefecture bordered enemy territory and needed strong defense, so Kuan was again made governor of Mian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 而州城埤狹，器械又少，寬知其難守，深以為憂。

translations.literal: But the prefectural city's walls were narrow and its weapons few; Kuan knew it would be hard to hold and was deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural walls were narrow and weapons scarce; Kuan knew the city would be hard to hold and was deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 又恐秋水暴長，陳人得乘其便。

translations.literal: He also feared that autumn waters would rise suddenly and the men of Chen would take advantage of the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: He also feared that autumn floods would rise suddenly and give Chen an opening.

sentences.zh: 卽白襄州總管，請戍兵，幷請移城於羊蹄山，權以避水。

translations.literal: He at once reported to the area commander of Xiang Prefecture, requesting garrison troops, and also requested to move the city to Yangti Mountain as a temporary measure to avoid the water.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately reported to the area commander of Xiang Prefecture, asking for garrison troops and permission to move the city temporarily to Yangti Mountain to escape the flood.

sentences.zh: 總管府許增兵守禦，不許遷移城。

translations.literal: The area commander's office approved additional troops for defense but did not approve moving the city.
translations.idiomatic: The area commander approved extra troops for defense but refused to move the city.

sentences.zh: 寬乃量度年常水至之處，豎大木於岸，以備船行。

translations.literal: Kuan then measured the place where the water ordinarily reached each year and set up large posts on the bank to mark the level for boat passage.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan then measured the usual high-water mark and set large posts on the bank to mark how high boats could pass.

sentences.zh: 襄州所遣兵未至，陳將程靈洗已率衆至於城下。

translations.literal: Before the troops sent from Xiang Prefecture had arrived, Chen general Cheng Lingxi had already led his host to the foot of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Before reinforcements from Xiang Prefecture arrived, Chen general Cheng Lingxi had already led his army to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 遂分佈戰艦，四面攻之。

translations.literal: He then deployed warships and attacked from all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Lingxi deployed warships and attacked from all four sides.

sentences.zh: 水勢猶小，靈洗未得近城。

translations.literal: The water was still low, and Lingxi could not yet approach the city.
translations.idiomatic: The water was still low, and Lingxi could not yet reach the walls.

sentences.zh: 寬每簡募驍兵，令夜掩擊，頻挫其銳。

translations.literal: Kuan each time selected and recruited fierce soldiers and ordered night raids, repeatedly blunting their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan repeatedly picked elite troops for night raids and blunted the enemy's momentum again and again.

sentences.zh: 相持旬日，靈洗無如之何。

translations.literal: They held each other for ten days, and Lingxi could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: The stalemate lasted ten days, and Lingxi could make no headway.

sentences.zh: 俄而雨水暴長，所豎木上，皆通船過。

translations.literal: Before long the rain waters rose suddenly; above the posts that had been set up, boats could all pass through.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the floodwaters surged; boats could pass above the markers Kuan had set.

sentences.zh: 靈洗乃以大艦臨逼，拍干打樓，應卽摧碎，弓弩大石，晝夜攻之。

translations.literal: Lingxi then pressed close with large ships; battering rams struck the towers and immediately smashed them; crossbows, catapults, and boulders attacked day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxi then pressed in with large ships; battering rams smashed the towers at once; crossbows, catapults, and boulders rained down day and night.

sentences.zh: 苦戰三十餘日，死傷過半。

translations.literal: After bitter fighting for more than thirty days, dead and wounded exceeded half.
translations.idiomatic: After more than thirty days of bitter fighting, casualties exceeded half the garrison.

sentences.zh: 女垣崩盡，陳人遂得上城。

translations.literal: The parapet walls collapsed completely, and the men of Chen were then able to ascend the city.
translations.idiomatic: The parapets collapsed entirely, and Chen troops were able to climb onto the walls.

sentences.zh: 短兵相拒，猶經二日。

translations.literal: At close quarters with short weapons they resisted each other for two more days.
translations.idiomatic: Hand-to-hand fighting on the walls continued for two more days.

sentences.zh: 外無繼援，力屈。

translations.literal: With no relief from outside, their strength gave way.
translations.idiomatic: With no relief from outside, the defenders were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 城陷之後，水便退縮。

translations.literal: After the city fell, the water then receded.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell, the floodwaters receded.

sentences.zh: 陳人乃執寬至揚州，尋被送嶺外。

translations.literal: The men of Chen then seized Kuan and took him to Yang Province; soon he was sent beyond the mountain ranges.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen forces seized Kuan and took him to Yang Province; soon he was sent beyond the Ling.

sentences.zh: 經數載，後還建業，遂卒於江左。

translations.literal: After several years he later returned to Jianye and then died in the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he returned to Jianye and died in the south.

sentences.zh: 時年六十七。

translations.literal: He was then sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子義宣後從禦正杜杲使于陳，始得將寬柩還。
