translations.literal: His son Yixuan later followed Chief Rectifier Du Gao on a mission to Chen and was only then able to bring Kuan's coffin back.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yixuan later accompanied Chief Rectifier Du Gao on a mission to Chen and was finally able to bring Kuan's coffin home.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，隋文帝詔贈襄郢二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang, Emperor Wen of Sui issued an edict posthumously appointing him governor of Xiang and E prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang Emperor Wen of Sui posthumously appointed him governor of Xiang and E prefectures.

sentences.zh: 義宣起家譙王儉府記室，轉司金二命士，合江令。

translations.literal: Yixuan began his career as recorder in the Prince of Qiao's household, then became a second-grade gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue, and was magistrate of Hejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan began as recorder in the household of the Prince of Qiao, then served as a second-grade gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue and as magistrate of Hejiang.

sentences.zh: 寬弟漢。

translations.literal: Kuan's younger brother Han.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan's younger brother was Han.

sentences.zh: 漢字仲霄，操尚弘雅，聰敏好學。

translations.literal: Han, styled Zhongxiao, was lofty and refined in conduct and bearing, clever and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Han, courtesy name Zhongxiao, was refined in conduct, clever, and fond of learning.

sentences.zh: 嘗見人作百字詩，一覽便誦。

translations.literal: Once he saw someone compose a hundred-character poem and, on one reading, could recite it.
translations.idiomatic: Once he saw someone compose a hundred-character poem and could recite it after a single reading.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武初，解褐員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei's reign, he left commoner status and was made assistant gentleman attendant at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei's reign he entered office as assistant gentleman attendant at leisure.

sentences.zh: 大統五年，除大丞相府士曹行參軍，補墨曹參軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Datong, he was appointed acting gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in the Grand Chancellor's office and was made up as gentleman of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Datong he was made acting gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in the grand chancellor's office and was assigned to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 漢善尺牘，尤便簿領，理識明贍，決斷如流。

translations.literal: Han was skilled at letters and especially adept at ledgers and registers; his reasoning was clear and ample, and his decisions flowed like water.
translations.idiomatic: Han was skilled at correspondence and especially adept at accounts; his judgment was clear and his decisions swift.

sentences.zh: 相府為之語曰：「日下粲爛有裴漢。

translations.literal: The chancellor's office had a saying about him: "Under the sun, brilliantly shining, there is Pei Han.
translations.idiomatic: A saying in the chancellor's office ran, "Under the sun there shines Pei Han.

sentences.zh: 」十一年，李遠出鎮弘農，啟漢為司馬。

translations.literal: " In the eleventh year, Li Yuan went out to command Hongnong and recommended Han as his chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Li Yuan went out to command Hongnong and recommended Han as his chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 遠特相器遇。

translations.literal: Yuan especially valued and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan valued and favored him especially.

sentences.zh: 尋加安東將軍、銀青光祿大夫、成都上士。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the added ranks of general who pacifies the east, grandee with the silver seal and blue ribbon, and senior gentleman of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the added titles of general who pacifies the east, grandee with the silver seal and blue ribbon, and senior gentleman of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 尋轉司車路下大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to lower grand master of the Directorate of Transport.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became lower grand master of the transport directorate.

sentences.zh: 與工部郭彥、太府高賓等參議格令，每較量時事，必有條理，彥等咸敬異之。

translations.literal: Together with Guo Yan of the Ministry of Works, Gao Bin of the Grand Storehouse, and others he deliberated on statutes and ordinances; whenever they weighed current affairs, he always had an orderly plan, and Yan and the others all respected and marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: With Guo Yan of the Ministry of Works, Gao Bin of the Grand Storehouse, and others he helped draft statutes and ordinances; whenever current policy was weighed, his proposals were always orderly, and Yan and the others all respected him.

sentences.zh: 加帥都督。

translations.literal: He was given the added rank of commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: They also named him commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 天和中，復與司宗孫恕、典祀薛慎同為八使，巡察風俗。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe period, he again served with Sun Shu of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan and Xue Shen of the Directorate of Sacrifices as one of the Eight Envoys inspecting local customs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhe period he again served with Sun Shu of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan and Xue Shen of the Directorate of Sacrifices as one of the Eight Envoys inspecting local customs.

sentences.zh: 五年，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was given the added ranks of grand general of the cavalry and status equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was given the added titles of grand general of the cavalry and status equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 子鏡民，少聰敏，涉獵經史。

translations.literal: His son Jingmin from youth was clever and keen, and ranged widely through the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingmin was clever from youth and read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 為大將軍、譚公會記室參軍。

translations.literal: He served as recorder for Grand General Duke of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: He kept the records for the Duke of Tan, grand general.

sentences.zh: 後歷宋王寔侍讀，轉記室，遷司錄。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as tutor to Prince Shi of Song, then recorder, and was promoted to chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as tutor to Prince Shi of Song, then as recorder, and was promoted to chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 宣政初，吏部上士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanzheng, he was senior gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xuanzheng he was senior gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 大象末，春官府都上士。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he was chief senior gentleman of the Spring Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Daxiang he was chief senior gentleman of the Spring Office.

sentences.zh: 漢弟尼。

translations.literal: Han's younger brother Ni.
translations.idiomatic: Han's younger brother was Ni.

sentences.zh: 漢弟尼

translations.literal: Han's younger brother Ni
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ni, Han's younger brother

sentences.zh: 尼字景尼，性弘雅，有器局。

translations.literal: Ni, styled Jingni, was by nature refined and magnanimous, with capacity and breadth of vision.
translations.idiomatic: Ni, courtesy name Jingni, was refined and magnanimous by nature, with breadth of vision.

sentences.zh: 起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: He began his career as court gentleman for attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as an attending court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 除梁王東閤祭酒，遷從事中郎，加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was appointed libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Prince of Liang, was promoted to attendant gentleman, and was given the added rank of regular attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Prince of Liang, promoted to attendant gentleman, and given the added rank of regular attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 隴西李際、范陽盧誕並有高名於世，與尼結忘年之交。

translations.literal: Li Ji of Longxi and Lu Dan of Fanyang both had high reputations in the world, and with Ni they formed friendships across the difference in age.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji of Longxi and Lu Dan of Fanyang both enjoyed great reputations, and Ni formed friendships with them despite the difference in age.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝元年，以本官從于謹平江陵，大獲軍實，謹恣諸將校取之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei, with his existing office he followed Yu Jin in pacifying Jiangling; they greatly obtained military stores, and Jin let the various officers and commanders take what they wished.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he followed Yu Jin in the pacification of Jiangling; the army seized vast stores, and Jin let the officers take what they wanted.

sentences.zh: 餘人皆競取珍玩，尼唯取梁元帝素琴一張而已。

translations.literal: The others all vied to take precious curios; Ni alone took one plain zither of Emperor Yuan of Liang, and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: While the others scrambled for jewels and curios, Ni took only one plain zither that had belonged to Emperor Yuan of Liang.

sentences.zh: 謹深歎美之。

translations.literal: Jin deeply sighed and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin praised him with deep admiration.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜御正下大夫。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed lower grand master in the Office of Rectification.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, Ni was made lower grand master in the Office of Rectification.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 贈輔國將軍、隨州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted General Who Assists the State and Governor of Sui Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made general who assists the state and governor of Sui Province.

sentences.zh: 子之隱，趙王招府記室參軍。

translations.literal: His son Zhiyin was recorder adjutant in the household of Prince Zhao, Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhiyin served as recorder adjutant in the household of Prince Zhao, Yuwen Zhao.

sentences.zh: 之隱弟師民，好學有識度，見稱于時。

translations.literal: Zhiyin's younger brother Shimin loved learning and had discernment and breadth; he was praised in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyin's younger brother Shimin loved learning and had real judgment; men of the day spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 起家秦王

translations.literal: He began his career under the Prince of Qin
translations.idiomatic: Shimin began his career in the household of the Prince of Qin

translations.literal: (Yun) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Yun]

sentences.zh: 〔贄〕府記室參軍，仍兼侍讀。

translations.literal: 〔Zhi〕 palace recorder adjutant, concurrently Reader.
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Zhi] household recorder adjutant, concurrently tutor to the prince.

sentences.zh: 寬族弟鴻。

translations.literal: Kuan's clansman Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kuan's clansman was Hong.

sentences.zh: 族弟鴻

translations.literal: Clansman Hong
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Hong

sentences.zh: 鴻少恭謹，有幹略，歷官內外。

translations.literal: Hong from youth was respectful and cautious, had administrative talent and stratagem, and served in posts both within and outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Hong was respectful and careful, capable in affairs, and served in posts at court and on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，拜輔城公司馬，加儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was appointed chief administrator of Fucheng company, with the added rank of equal in three departments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Hong was made chief administrator of Fucheng company, with the added rank of equal in three departments.

sentences.zh: 為晉公護雍州治中，累遷御正中大夫，進位開府儀同三司，轉民部中大夫。

translations.literal: He served as chief administrator of Yong Province under Duke of Jin Hu, was repeatedly promoted to middle grand master in the Office of Rectification, advanced to opening-office equal in three departments, and transferred to middle grand master of the Ministry of Peoples.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Yong Province chief administrator under Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, rose to middle grand master in the Office of Rectification, was promoted to opening-office equal in three departments, and transferred to middle grand master of the Ministry of Peoples.

sentences.zh: 保定末，出為中州刺史、九曲城主。

translations.literal: At the end of Baoding, he went out as Governor of Zhong Province and commandant of Nine-bend Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Baoding era he was sent out as governor of Zhong Province and commandant of Nine-bend Fortress.

sentences.zh: 鎮守邊鄙，甚有扞禦之能。

translations.literal: Holding the frontier garrison, he had very great ability to resist and defend.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier he showed great skill in defense.

sentences.zh: 衛公直出鎮襄州，以鴻為襄州司馬。

translations.literal: Duke of Wei Zhi went out to command Xiang Province; Hong was made chief administrator of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Wei Yuwen Zhi went out to command Xiang Province, Hong was made his chief administrator there.

sentences.zh: 天和初，拜郢州刺史，轉襄州總管府長史，賜爵高邑縣侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe, he was appointed Governor of Ying Province, was transferred to chief of staff of the Xiang Province Governor-General's headquarters, and was granted the title Marquis of Gaoyi county.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianhe he was made governor of Ying Province, then transferred to chief of staff at Xiang Province headquarters, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoyi county.

sentences.zh: 從直南征，軍敗，遂沒。

translations.literal: Following Zhi on the southern campaign, the army was defeated, and he was thereupon captured.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yuwen Zhi on the southern campaign; when the army was defeated, he was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於陳。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died in Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in Chen captivity.

sentences.zh: 朝廷哀之，贈豐資遂三州刺史。

translations.literal: The court grieved for him and posthumously granted him Governor of the three provinces Feng, Zi, and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: The court mourned him and posthumously made him governor of Feng, Zi, and Sui provinces.

sentences.zh: 楊敷字文衍，華山公寬之兄子也。

translations.literal: Yang Fu, styled Wenyuan, was a nephew of Duke of Huashan Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu, courtesy name Wenyuan, was a nephew of Pei Kuan, Duke of Huashan.

sentences.zh: 父暄，字景和。

translations.literal: His father Xuanchun, styled Jinghe.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuanchun, courtesy name Jinghe.

sentences.zh: 性朗悟，有識學。

translations.literal: By nature he was bright and perceptive, with knowledge and learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was bright and perceptive by nature and well versed in learning.

sentences.zh: 弱冠拜奉朝請，歷員外散騎侍郎、華州別駕、尚書右中兵郎中、輔國將軍、諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At age twenty he was appointed court gentleman for attendance; he successively served as assistant attendant-in-ordinary of scattered cavalry, vice governor of Hua Province, right middle bureau director of soldiers in the Secretariat, general who assists the state, and adviser on remonstrance and counsel.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he entered service as court gentleman for attendance and later served as assistant attendant-in-ordinary of scattered cavalry, vice governor of Hua Province, right middle bureau director of soldiers in the Secretariat, general who assists the state, and remonstrance and counsel grandee.

sentences.zh: 以別將從魏廣陽王深征葛榮，為榮所害。

translations.literal: As a separate commander he followed Prince of Guangyang Shen of Wei in campaigning against Ge Rong, and was killed by Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as a detached commander under Prince of Guangyang Yuan Shen of Wei against Ge Rong, he was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 贈殿中尚書、華夏二州諸軍事、鎮西將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Director of the Palace Secretariat, military affairs for Hua and Xia two provinces, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made director of the palace secretariat, area commander of military affairs for Hua and Xia provinces, general who pacifies the west, and governor of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進爵為侯，增邑幷前八百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was advanced in rank to marquis and his fief was increased together with the former by eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Fu was raised to marquis and his fief, together with what he already held, was increased by eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 除小載師下大夫，使北豫州迎司馬消難，還，授使持節、蒙州諸軍事、蒙州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed lower grand master of the Lesser Master of Carriages, sent to Northern Yu Province to welcome Sima Xiaonan; on return, he was given bearer of the staff, military affairs for Meng Province, and Governor of Meng Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made lower grand master of the Lesser Master of Carriages and sent to Northern Yu Province to welcome Sima Xiaonan; on his return he received bearer of the staff, military affairs for Meng Province, and the governorship of Meng Province.

sentences.zh: 先是蠻左等多受齊假署，數為亂逆。

translations.literal: Earlier, the southern barbarian peoples for the most part had received provisional appointments from Qi and repeatedly acted in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Before this the southern tribes had largely accepted provisional appointments from Northern Qi and had often rebelled.

sentences.zh: 敷推誠布信，隨方慰撫，蠻左等感之，相率歸附。

translations.literal: Fu spread sincerity and good faith, comforted and soothed each according to its place, and the barbarian peoples were moved by this and came over in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Fu treated them with sincerity and good faith, soothing each group in turn; the tribes were won over and submitted in succession.

sentences.zh: 敷乃送其首四十餘人赴闕，請因齊所假而授之。

translations.literal: Fu thereupon sent more than forty of their chieftains to the capital and requested that they be granted office according to what Qi had provisionally given them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu then sent more than forty of their chieftains to the capital and asked that they be given office on the same terms Qi had used.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻等愈更感悅，州境獲寧。

translations.literal: The various barbarians were the more moved and pleased; the province's territory obtained peace.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes were still more grateful, and order was restored throughout the province.

sentences.zh: 特降璽書勞問，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: An imperial sealed letter was specially sent to express sympathy and inquiry; he was given the added ranks of grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal in three departments.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent a special sealed letter of commendation and added the titles grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal in three departments.

sentences.zh: 保定中，徵為司水中大夫。

translations.literal: In the Baoding period, he was summoned as middle grand master in the Directorate of Water.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoding era he was recalled to serve as middle grand master in the Directorate of Water.

sentences.zh: 夷夏吏民，乃荊州總管長孫儉並表請留之。

translations.literal: Barbarian and Han officials and commoners, and also Grand Marshal of Jing Province Yuwen Jian, jointly memorialized requesting that he be kept in place.
translations.idiomatic: Han and tribal officials and people alike, along with Jing Province grand marshal Yuwen Jian, jointly petitioned to keep him in office.

sentences.zh: 時議欲東討，將委敷以舟艦轉輸之事，故弗許焉。

translations.literal: At the time the court planned an eastern campaign and intended to entrust Fu with transport by boats and ships; therefore the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then planning an eastern campaign and meant to put Fu in charge of river transport, so the petitions were denied.

sentences.zh: 陳公純鎮陝

translations.literal: Duke of Chen Chun was stationed at Shan
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Chen Yuwen Chun took command at Shan

translations.literal: (West) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: West]

sentences.zh: 〔州〕，以敷為總管長史。

translations.literal: 〔Province〕, and made Fu chief of staff of the governor-general headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: xi Province headquarters, Fu was made chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉司木中大夫、軍器副監。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was transferred to middle grand master in the Directorate of Wood and deputy overseer of the Arsenal.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to middle grand master in the Directorate of Wood and deputy overseer of the arsenal.

sentences.zh: 敷明習吏事，所在以勤察著名，每歲奏課居最，累獲優賞。

translations.literal: Fu clearly understood administrative affairs; wherever he was, he was famed for diligence and scrutiny; each year in performance reports he ranked first, and repeatedly received outstanding rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Fu knew administrative work thoroughly; wherever he served he was noted for diligence and vigilance; year after year his performance reports ranked first, and he was repeatedly singled out for reward.

sentences.zh: 進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to grand general of agile cavalry and opening-office equal in three departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand general of agile cavalry and opening-office equal in three departments.

sentences.zh: 天和六年，出為汾州諸軍事、汾州刺史，進爵為公，增邑一千五百戶。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhe, he went out as area commander of military affairs for Fen Province and Governor of Fen Province; he was advanced in rank to duke, and his fief was increased by one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianhe he was sent out as area commander of military affairs for Fen Province and governor of Fen, raised to duke, and given an added fief of one thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 齊將段孝先率衆五萬來寇，梯沖地道，晝夜攻城。

translations.literal: Qi general Duan Xiaoxian led a host of fifty thousand to invade; with scaling ladders, rams, and underground tunnels, they assaulted the city day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi general Duan Xiaoxian led fifty thousand men against the city with siege towers, rams, and underground tunnels, attacking day and night.

sentences.zh: 敷親當矢石，隨事扞禦，拒守累旬。

translations.literal: Fu personally faced arrows and stones, resisted according to each circumstance, and held out for many tens of days.
translations.idiomatic: Fu met arrows and stones in person, met each assault as it came, and held out for many weeks.

sentences.zh: 孝先攻之愈急。

translations.literal: Xiaoxian attacked all the more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Xiaoxian pressed the attack ever harder.

sentences.zh: 時城中兵不滿二千，戰死者已十四五，糧儲又盡，公私窮蹙。

translations.literal: At the time the troops in the city numbered fewer than two thousand; those killed in battle already reached four or five tenths; grain stores were again exhausted, and public and private both were in desperate straits.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison held fewer than two thousand men; four or five men in ten had already fallen; grain was gone, and public stores and private households alike were desperate.

sentences.zh: 齊公憲總兵赴救，憚孝先，不敢進軍。

translations.literal: Duke of Qi Xian mustered troops to go to the rescue, but feared Xiaoxian and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian marched to the relief but feared Duan Xiaoxian and would not press forward.

sentences.zh: 敷知必陷沒，乃召其衆謂之曰：「吾與卿等，俱在邊鎮，實願同心戮力，破賊全城。

translations.literal: Fu knew the city must fall, so he summoned his men and said to them: "You and I together are stationed on the frontier; I truly wish to join hearts and combine strength to break the enemy and preserve the whole city.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the city could not hold, Fu gathered his men and said, "You and I stand together on the frontier; I had hoped we might unite and break the enemy to save this city.

sentences.zh: 但強寇四面攻圍日久，吾等糧食已盡，救援斷絕。

translations.literal: But strong enemies have attacked from all sides for many days; our grain is already exhausted, and relief is cut off.
translations.idiomatic: But a strong foe has besieged us from every side for days; our grain is spent and no relief will come.

sentences.zh: 守死窮城，非丈夫也。

translations.literal: To hold out and die in a hopeless city is not the act of a true man.
translations.idiomatic: To die defending a doomed city is no true man's course.

sentences.zh: 今勝兵之士，猶數百人，欲突圍出戰，死生一決。

translations.literal: Today the fit fighting men still number several hundred; I wish to break through the siege and go out to fight, settling life and death in one decision.
translations.idiomatic: We still have several hundred able fighters; I mean to break out and fight, staking life and death on a single charge.

sentences.zh: 儻或得免，猶冀生還，受罪闕庭，孰與死於寇乎！

translations.literal: If by chance we may escape, we may still hope to return alive, receive punishment before the imperial court — how is that not better than dying at the hands of the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: If we can break free, some of us may yet live, return home, and accept judgment at court—better that than dying at the enemy's hands!

sentences.zh: 吾計決矣，於諸君意何如？

translations.literal: My decision is made — what do you all think?
translations.idiomatic: My mind is made up. What say you?

sentences.zh: 」衆咸涕泣從命。

translations.literal: " All wept and, weeping, obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: " All wept and agreed to follow him.

sentences.zh: 敷乃率見兵夜出，擊殺齊軍數十人。

translations.literal: Fu then led the troops available and went out by night, killing several tens of Qi soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: That night Fu led his remaining men out and killed several dozen Qi soldiers.

sentences.zh: 齊軍衆稍卻。

translations.literal: The Qi army masses withdrew slightly.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ranks fell back a little.

sentences.zh: 俄而孝先率諸軍盡銳圍之，敷殊死戰，矢盡，為孝先所擒。

translations.literal: Before long Xiaoxian led all the armies with full sharpness to surround them; Fu fought to the death; arrows exhausted, he was captured by Xiaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Duan Xiaoxian closed in with every available man; Fu fought to the last; when his arrows were spent he was taken.

sentences.zh: 齊人方欲任用之，敷不為之屈，遂以憂懼卒於鄴。

translations.literal: The men of Qi were just then intending to employ him, but Fu would not submit to them; he thereupon died in Ye from grief and fear.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi meant to win him over, but Fu would not yield and died in Ye of grief and anguish.

sentences.zh: 高祖平齊，贈使持節、大將軍、淮廣復三州諸軍事、三州刺史，諡曰忠壯。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor pacified Qi, he was posthumously granted bearer of the staff, Grand General, military affairs for Huai, Guang, and Fu three provinces, Governor of three provinces, and the posthumous name Loyal and Robust.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu pacified Qi, Fu was posthumously made bearer of the staff, grand general, area commander of military affairs for Huai, Guang, and Fu provinces, governor of those three provinces, and given the posthumous name Zhongzhuang.

sentences.zh: 葬於華陰舊塋。

translations.literal: He was buried at the old family graves at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried in the family graveyard at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 子素，有文武材略。

translations.literal: His son Su had both civil and military talent and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: His son Su possessed both civil and military gifts.

sentences.zh: 大象末，上柱國、清河郡公。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he was a pillar of state and Duke of Qinghe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era he held the rank of pillar of state and Duke of Qinghe commandery.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自三方鼎峙，羣雄競逐，俊能馳騖，各吠非主。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Since the three realms stood in threefold confrontation, rival heroes competed in pursuit; talented men galloped freely, each barking at a lord not his own.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Once the three realms stood in threefold balance, rival heroes raced to seize advantage; gifted men rushed from side to side, each serving whoever would have him.

sentences.zh: 爭奮厲其智勇，思赴蹈于仁義。

translations.literal: They strove to exert their wisdom and courage, thinking to devote and throw themselves into humanity and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: They strained every wit and nerve, hoping to give themselves wholly to loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 臨危不顧，前哲所難。

translations.literal: Facing peril without turning back — this the sages of old found hard.
translations.idiomatic: To face peril without flinching is what even the ancients found hard.

sentences.zh: 趙善等或行彰于孝友，或誠顯於忠概，咸躬志力，俱徇功名。

translations.literal: Zhao Shan and the like — some showed conduct manifest in filial piety and friendship, some showed sincerity manifest in loyal integrity; all personally applied mind and strength and alike pursued fame and merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shan and men like him showed filial conduct or fierce integrity; each gave body and mind alike in pursuit of honor.

sentences.zh: 兵凶戰危，城孤援絕。

translations.literal: War is baleful and battle dangerous; the city alone, relief cut off.
translations.idiomatic: War is cruel and battle perilous; a city stands alone and relief never comes.

sentences.zh: 楊敷、趙善，類龐德之勢窮；

translations.literal: Yang Fu and Zhao Shan resemble Pang De when his strength was exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu and Zhao Shan were like Pang De when his strength was spent;

sentences.zh: 元定、裴寬，同黃權之無路。

translations.literal: Yuan Ding and Pei Kuan are the same as Huang Quan with no way out.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ding and Pei Kuan, like Huang Quan, had nowhere left to turn.

sentences.zh: 王旅不振，非其罪也。

translations.literal: The royal armies did not recover — this was not their fault.
translations.idiomatic: That the royal armies failed to save them was no fault of their own.

sentences.zh: 敷少而慷慨，終能立節，仁而有勇，其最優乎。

translations.literal: Fu from youth was generous-spirited; in the end he could uphold integrity; benevolent and yet brave — is he not the finest among them?
translations.idiomatic: Fu was generous-spirited from youth and in the end kept his integrity—benevolent and brave; among them he stands first.

sentences.zh: 楊摽屢有奇功，狃於數勝，輕敵無備，兵破身囚，未能遠謀，良可嗟矣。

translations.literal: Yang Biao repeatedly had singular achievements, but grew accustomed to repeated victories, took the enemy lightly and made no preparations; his army was broken and his body captured — he could not plan far ahead; truly this is lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Biao won startling victories again and again but grew reckless with success, took the enemy lightly and left himself unguarded—his army was shattered and he was taken captive. He could not see far enough ahead; that is truly lamentable.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「師出以律，否臧凶。

translations.literal: The Changes says: "An army goes forth by rule; if the rule is not good, misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, "An army must march by discipline; without it, ruin follows."

sentences.zh: 」《傳》曰：「不備不虞，不可以師。

translations.literal: " The Commentary says: "Without preparing against the unforeseen, one may not take the field."
translations.idiomatic: " The Commentary says, "Without guarding against the unexpected, one must not take the field."

sentences.zh: 」其楊摽之謂也？

translations.literal: " Is this not what is meant concerning Yang Biao?
translations.idiomatic: " Is that not the lesson of Yang Biao?

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
